# Native Ubuntu protocol fields and Debian xt comments

These disposable VM observations were captured by PR #8 workflow run
`41340962736`, source commit `ff76ed1911bebb52a96447c655a0b943ae7b55f0`, tree
`055aceec00d87fbaa0a1e4ee778bb8fbc908cee6`. No machine IDs, credentials or signed
download URLs are present in the fixture files.

## Ubuntu 24.04 baseline

Prefix: `ufw-ubuntu2404-pr8-2026-11-01.`. All three files are unchanged captured
command outputs, originally named `initial-nft.json`, `initial-iptables.txt`
and `initial-ip6tables.txt`.

- Job `124950662046`, artifact `13097059176`.
- ZIP: 115861 bytes, SHA-256
  `404e685a6691b9e41bb93613d6516cc441f9a2de0442912d8e412dbab7f01a15`.
- UFW `0.36.2`, nftables `1.0.9`, iptables/ip6tables `1.8.10 (nf_tables)`.

| Suffix | Bytes | SHA-256 |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `nft.json` | 52982 | `f204f981f0e810818cd63dbad81254666832104952d63ef071de2764d0a01ea9` |
| `iptables.txt` | 4503 | `cc968b7a0d0f049c91e1902c1b9970cffa86e38038262370e8e098a628b41ace` |
| `ip6tables.txt` | 8125 | `72caee751e35ca8c3747c1ebdb833af86a63e64d69b9ba000a9a4a5b72b345ae` |

The native snapshot contains ten IPv4 `payload ip protocol` comparisons: eight
ICMP clauses and two TCP/UDP output clauses. The previous strict projection
rejected the first such comparison and truthfully returned manual/partial. The
new regression preserves the original graph and supports only this exact IPv4
field with known symbolic values and equality. IPv6 `nexthdr`, other fields,
unsupported operators and ambiguous operand shapes remain outside this support.

## Debian 12 owned ACCEPT

Prefix: `ufw-debian12-owned-accept-pr8-2026-11-01.`. The JSON is the unchanged
`firewall-audit-allow-all.nft.json`. The two text files contain the exact decoded
`runtime.ipv4` and `runtime.ipv6` strings from the contemporaneous
`firewall-audit-allow-all.state.json`; no newline was added to either string.

- Job `124950661806`, artifact `13097381543`.
- ZIP: 122185 bytes, SHA-256
  `eefd6fdc00ecb6ea1fc6473541fdc4db955ee6456a71c17cb3306c2e1cea18fe`.
- UFW `0.36.2`, nftables `1.0.6`, iptables/ip6tables `1.8.9 (nf_tables)`.

| Suffix | Bytes | SHA-256 |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `nft.json` | 53189 | `5257c444f57feac0cfa0ecfcb1f084e27fd8e7d9ce0c3222842afe0840119b12` |
| `iptables.txt` | 4590 | `338c2c7c4b995693c331e0bde38ab24070985b90f4168254c62faf148b9cad4b` |
| `ip6tables.txt` | 8212 | `2e2d6dc55ba0536ff21d287ae50d54ec0a8411ac55e0a91b4df6f10a2b2a47b6` |

The two real owned INPUT rules contain an opaque `xt comment` expression,
counter and ACCEPT, with no native `rule.comment` metadata. Kernel `xt_comment`
is an unconditional no-op match. Its text is not reconstructed and it does not
enable generic xt support. The original graph proves unconditional early ACCEPT
even when optional conntrack enrichment is unavailable. The native job stopped
at a harness correlation assertion before running the allow-all audit, then
removed its owned rules; this fixture replay is not an assertion that that job
completed its audit gate.

## Replay scope and primary semantics

The regression's netlink generation replies are controlled transport fixtures.
Ubuntu's added ACCEPT and restored cases are labelled synthetic deltas around
its actual baseline. Debian's separate owned-ACCEPT snapshot was actually
captured after insertion. New native acceptance still requires CI.

- [Official nftables IPv4 header and protocol documentation](https://www.netfilter.org/projects/nftables/manpage.html), section IPV4 HEADER EXPRESSION.
- [Official nftables protocol and IPv6 extension-header distinction](https://wiki.nftables.org/wiki-nftables/index.php/Matching_packet_header_fields).
- [Linux v6.8 xt_comment.c](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v6.8/net/netfilter/xt_comment.c), blob `f095557e3ef6f3563883937863716470bb1b3ad9`: `comment_mt` always returns true.
